title: Symmetric presentation conormal exact sequence over the free locus
statement:
Let $P$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\subseteq P$ with $m\geq0$, $A=P/I$, $M=I/I^2$, $q:A^{\oplus m}\twoheadrightarrow M$ given by $e_j\mapsto[g_j]$, and $K=\ker q$. Put $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ with canonical map $\iota:M\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Let $Q=P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\varphi:Q\twoheadrightarrow C$ send coefficients through $P\to A\to C$ and $y_j\mapsto\iota([g_j])$, and $J=\ker\varphi$. Let $h\in C$, $T=C[1/h]$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and suppose that for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset T$, with contraction $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the module $M_{\mathfrak p}=A_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_A M$ is finite free over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $M\otimes_A T$ and $K\otimes_A T$ are finite projective $T$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and coefficient reduction modulo $I$ induces a split short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow M\otimes_A T\xrightarrow{\alpha}(J/J^2)\otimes_C T\xrightarrow{\beta}K\otimes_A T\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $\alpha([g]\otimes t)=[g]\otimes t$ for $g\in I$. More explicitly, put $L=\ker(A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C)$ and $\ell(k)=\sum_j k_j y_j$ for $k=(k_j)\in K$. The map $K\otimes_A T\to(L/L^2)\otimes_C T$, $k\otimes t\mapsto[\ell(k)]\otimes t$, is an isomorphism, and $\beta$ is reduction $Q\to A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ on conormal classes followed by its inverse. Also the base change of $q$ gives a split short exact sequence $0\to K\otimes_A T\to T^{\oplus m}\to M\otimes_A T\to0$. No projectivity of $M$ on all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), proof, equation-sequence and equation-sequence-localized (lines 357–418), restricted to an arbitrary affine open over the locally free locus of I/I². The projective calculation is local on Spec A; the general 07EV conormal-isomorphism claim is not used away from that locus. Compare Elkik II, Lemma 3, printed pp.562–564, https://www.numdam.org/item/10.24033/asens.1258.pdf (archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: Write $M_T=M\otimes_A T$ and $K_T=K\otimes_A T$. The ring $A=P/I$ is Noetherian by the finite-type permanence lemma. Since $K\subseteq A^m$, the Noetherian submodule lemma gives finitely many generators of $K$. Thus $A^s\to A^m\xrightarrow{q}M\to0$ is a finite presentation. Tensor right exactness gives $T^s\to T^m\xrightarrow{q_T}M_T\to0$, so $M_T$ is finitely presented, and also $K_T\to T^m\to M_T\to0$ is right exact. No injectivity of $K_T\to T^m$ has yet been claimed.

Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $T$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$, $\widetilde{\mathfrak p}=(P\to A)^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, and $S=P\setminus\widetilde{\mathfrak p}$. Write $P'=S^{-1}P$, $I'=S^{-1}I$ and $A'=A_{\mathfrak p}=P'/I'$. Exact localization identifies $I'/I'^2$ with $M_{\mathfrak p}=:M'$ and $\ker(A'^m\to M')$ with $K_{\mathfrak p}=:K'$; here localization of ideal squares follows from extension commuting with powers. Symmetric base change identifies $C'=S^{-1}C$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_{A'}M'$. Coefficientwise fractions identify $S^{-1}Q=P'[y]$ and $S^{-1}(A[y])=A'[y]$; for example $\sum_j(a_j/s_j)y^j$ is the fraction with denominator $\prod_js_j$ obtained by multiplying its finitely many coefficients to that denominator. Exact localization then identifies their presentation kernels with $S^{-1}J$ and $S^{-1}L$, and their conormals with $S^{-1}(J/J^2)$ and $S^{-1}(L/L^2)$. All identifications send a numerator class to that same class over denominator one.

source.place: Tags 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization); coefficientwise localization of the finite polynomials.

proof.text: The hypothesis makes $M'$ finite free, hence projective: its finite basis identifies it with a finite free module, which is its own direct summand. Apply the projective coefficient-reduction exactness theorem to $(P',I',q_{\mathfrak p})$ and the projective symmetric-presentation conormal equivalence to $(A',M',q_{\mathfrak p})$. They give an exact row $0\to C'\otimes_{A'}M'\to S^{-1}(J/J^2)\to S^{-1}(L/L^2)\to0$ and the isomorphism $C'\otimes_{A'}K'\cong S^{-1}(L/L^2)$, with the stated coefficient and linear-form formulas. The surjection $q_{\mathfrak p}$ splits since $M'$ is projective. Tensoring the section and retraction identities with $T_{\mathfrak q}$ therefore gives an injective $K'\otimes_{A'}T_{\mathfrak q}\to T_{\mathfrak q}^m$, without a flatness hypothesis on $A'\to T_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), equation-sequence on the projective locus; Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective).

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak r$ be the contraction of $\mathfrak q$ to $C'$. The map $C'\to T_{\mathfrak q}$ is localization at $C'\setminus\mathfrak r$: a fraction from $C$ or $T=C_h$ has a denominator outside the corresponding contracted prime, and conversely every element outside $\mathfrak r$ becomes invertible. The universal properties of these rings of fractions give inverse maps fixing $C$. Thus exact localization of the row and equivalence of step 3 gives the same row and linear-form equivalence over $T_{\mathfrak q}$. Localization commutes with the tensors by the cited tensor-localization theorem. Associativity identifications here send $(m/s)\otimes t$ to $m\otimes s^{-1}t$, with inverse $m\otimes t\mapsto(m/1)\otimes t$. In particular the first arrow is $[g]\otimes t\mapsto[g]\otimes t$, and reduction is $[z]\otimes t\mapsto[\bar z]\otimes t$. This checks the actual maps, as well as the modules.

source.place: Tags 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization); the rings-of-fractions universal property and explicit tensor formulas.

proof.text: Construct the global maps before descending their properties. Polynomial coefficient conormal inclusion gives $i:M\otimes_A C\to J/J^2$ with $i([g]\otimes c)=c[g]$. Coefficient reduction sends $J$ into $L$ and $J^2$ into $L^2$, hence gives $r:J/J^2\to L/L^2$. Its composite with $i$ is zero because constants from $I$ reduce to zero. The corrected symmetric-algebra conormal statement supplies the well-defined map $\lambda:K\otimes_A C\to L/L^2$, $k\otimes c\mapsto c[\ell(k)]$. Tensor these three maps with $T$ to get $i_T,r_T,\lambda_T$. The tensor universal property gives precisely their formulas in the question. Localizing these formulas at $\mathfrak q$ gives the maps of step 4: coefficient reduction fixes the variables and acts only on coefficients, and $\ell(k)/s=\ell(k/s)$. Thus $(i_T)_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective, its image is $\ker(r_T)_{\mathfrak q}$, $(r_T)_{\mathfrak q}$ is surjective and $(\lambda_T)_{\mathfrak q}$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), coefficient reduction; Tag 07EV (lemma-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra), only the corrected linear-form map, not its false unrestricted injectivity.

proof.text: The preceding local properties imply the global properties by the following elementary annihilator test. If a nonzero element $x$ of any $T$-module vanished in every maximal localization, choose a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator. Vanishing there gives $s x=0$ with $s$ outside that maximal ideal, contradicting containment of the annihilator. Apply this to $\ker i_T$, $\ker\lambda_T$, $\operatorname{coker}\lambda_T$, $\operatorname{coker}r_T$, and $\ker r_T/\operatorname{im}i_T$. Exact localization identifies their localizations with the defects just shown to vanish. Apply it also to the kernel of $K_T\to T^m$, which vanishes by step 3 and the tensor identifications of step 4. Consequently $\lambda_T$ is an isomorphism, $0\to M_T\xrightarrow{i_T}(J/J^2)\otimes_C T\xrightarrow{r_T}(L/L^2)\otimes_C T\to0$ is exact, and $0\to K_T\to T^m\xrightarrow{q_T}M_T\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local), annihilator argument written out; Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact).

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $T$, the tensor identifications of step 4 give $(M_T)_{\mathfrak q}=M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}T_{\mathfrak q}$, finite free by the hypothesis: tensor its finite basis and inverse coordinate map. Since $M_T$ is finitely presented by step 1, the local criterion gives that $M_T$ is finite projective. The exact row with $q_T$ therefore splits. Its retraction $\rho:T^m\to K_T$ makes $K_T$ a direct summand of $T^m$, so it is projective by the definition's direct-summand characterization and finite because the $m$ elements $\rho(e_j)$ generate it. This proves both finiteness/projectivity assertions and the last split exact row.

Set $\alpha=i_T$ and $\beta=\lambda_T^{-1}r_T$. Step 6 and the isomorphism $\lambda_T$ give exactly the displayed short exact sequence and its specified coefficient-reduction map. Since $K_T$ is projective by step 7, the short exact sequence splits. No choices in this splitting change $\alpha$, $\beta$ or $\lambda_T$. If $T=0$ (including $I=P$ or nilpotent $h$), all displayed $T$-modules are zero and all conclusions hold; the annihilator argument has no nonzero element to consider. If $m=0$, then $I=M=K=J=L=0$, and the same formulas give the zero sequences.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07CE, equation-sequence, localized at contractions of primes of T; extension to an arbitrary principal open and explicit descent written by Q25. Uses the existing corrected projective nodes instead of the false unrestricted injectivity in 07EV.

The statement is unchanged from live apart from backslashes, and there is no repair note, so this is an ordinary split. It is true: I checked T=0, m=0, the case k[e]/(e^2) with I=(e), redundant generators, and that the 07EV counterexample is excluded by the free-locus hypothesis. Step 2 localizes at S=P minus the preimage of p; S^{-1}A=A_p (00CT), and Nagata gives (J^2)Q'=(JQ')^2. Step 3: the projective reduction-exact and linear-form equivalence nodes apply to (P',I',q_p), and the split q_p gives injectivity after tensoring without flatness. Step 4: T_q=C_{r0} is a localization of C'. Step 5 builds the global i, r and lambda from coefficient-inclusion, 07EV(2) and the tensor universal property, and they agree on generators with the local maps. Step 6 is the 00HN annihilator test, fairly marked elementary. Step 7: M_T is finitely presented and locally free, so it is finite projective by 00NX, and K_T is a direct summand of T^m. Step 8: beta = lambda_T^{-1} r_T, split because K_T is projective. Batch 5: lem-trf-finite-projective-local-free is a Mathlib leaf (Module.projective_of_localization_maximal, 00NX) with no proof deps, generic algebra outside both assumptions, so accepted.
